hook_text: A flag with no official meaning for its colours, a motto in a language nobody speaks today, and an anthem in five languages. Why?
clip_script: Monday assembly in Mahikeng. The flag rises up the pole: red, white, green, gold, black and blue, joined in a Y shape that flows into one band. The coat of arms shows a rising sun, a secretary bird, a protea and two figures from ancient rock art, with a San motto meaning diverse people unite. The anthem joins two songs and five languages. Every symbol says the same thing: many people, one nation.
visual_style: Whiteboard flag unfurling on a pole, then the coat of arms built up layer by layer from the motto to the rising sun, then musical notes in five colours flowing into one line.
mood: Proud and warm, like a school assembly on Heritage Day.
pacing: One symbol at a time, building each piece slowly and explaining its meaning.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and draw the coat of arms, labelling five of its parts.
